synth.title: Pre-delivery self-walk gate
synth.principle_summary: A self-review checklist changes behavior only when it is structurally mandatory, not advisory: formal HCI inspection methods (heuristic evaluation, Nielsen and Molich 1990, paired with the 0-4 severity scale from Nielsen's later work) and the cognitive walkthrough (Wharton, Rieman, Lewis and Polson 1994) both convert "does this feel right" into a fixed ordered set of answerable questions, and the strongest outcome evidence that mandatory beats optional is outside UX entirely: the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist trial (Haynes et al., NEJM 2009) dropped complications from 11.0% to 7.0% and in-hospital mortality from 1.5% to 0.8% purely by making an ordered checklist required before a procedure, not by writing better advice. Real software now builds this same shape as live product surface, not just theory: Vercel's Production Checklist panel, GitHub/GitLab/Graphite's merge gates, and Deputy's onboarding review all block the primary commit action until every sub-check reports a true state, and each reports its sub-checks as independently truthful rows (some pass, some explicitly "not configured") rather than one aggregate score. CI tooling goes further and makes the gate literally mechanical: Chromatic and Percy hold a PR's merge status at "pending" until every visual diff is explicitly approved or rejected, so the checklist is not text a reviewer can skim past, it is a block on the action itself. Uber's Base Counter plus its "Feature Review Readiness" step shows the two-stage pattern this stream should adopt: automated scoring runs continuously (daily CD builds, auto-ticket on violation), and a human (or, for Solen, the agent's own final message) only confirms the machine's findings rather than doing a fresh freeform look each time. The generalizable principle for Solen: encode the six-axis self-walk (squint, hierarchy count, type-size ceiling, grouping tree, contrast math, density) as a Stop-hook gate that requires all six lines to report PASS before a turn claiming a UI delivery can end, each line independently truthful and individually fixable, exactly the shape real merge gates and the WHO checklist already prove works and the design-QA industry (Figma's native AI reviewer, the 2026 "AI design crit before human review" workflow trend, Eleken's 17-step pre-handoff checklist) is independently converging on as of 2026.
synth.generative_prior:
MECHANIZE spec, not a rendering default: the "right first mockup" here IS the gate firing correctly. Metric + formula + threshold per axis, each grounded against a real precedent that proves the shape works in production:

1. squint (<=8 words, must name the stated primary task target) -- precedent: Vercel's Production Checklist shows a live "4/6" counter with each item struck-through only once truly done, proving a compact single-line-per-check format reads clearly at delivery time.
2. hierarchy (N = distinct type sizes visible; FLAG if N>3, or >2 elements stack bold+color+size at once) -- precedent: Shopify Polaris's reduction litmus ("could this header, subcopy, and button just be a button?") is the real-world version of the same discipline, one dominant element/action per section.
3. type-ceiling (largest:second-largest ratio; FLAG if <1.3, i.e. the 30% dominance-jump floor, or if any delta is 1-2px) -- Solen's own T3 researched floor, unchanged from baseline.
4. grouping (state peers-list / peers-cards / facets-whitespace / facets-card-dividers + one line why; FLAG on a full-width tinted "stopping point" or card-in-card) -- unchanged from baseline decision tree.
5. contrast (measured ratio per new text/bg pair; FLAG below 4.5:1 WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3, or below APCA Lc 75 on sunken/dark surfaces) -- T1, unchanged.
6. density (the existing FLOORS LAW 5-pass: photo focal, one biggest element, real number, semantic-color moment, no dead-grey zone) -- unchanged from baseline.

THRESHOLD FOR THE GATE ITSELF (new, from the scouting reports): all 6 lines must report PASS before the turn can end -- an all-or-nothing bar, not a majority. Precedent: Deputy's onboarding review keeps the "Review and submit" CTA disabled-grey until 100% of the left-column checklist is green, not some percentage. Each of the 6 lines must be independently truthful (a line can say "not applicable this turn" but never be silently omitted or folded into a single aggregate pass/fail) -- precedent: GitLab's merge-request panel and Graphite's PR sidebar both keep the merge-readiness gate and the approval gate as two SEPARATE rows rather than one combined verdict, and Graphite explicitly shows a neutral "not configured" state distinct from pass/fail, which is the model for a self-walk axis that genuinely doesn't apply this turn. The gate itself must BLOCK the action (exit code 2 stopping the turn), not just print advisory text -- precedent: Chromatic/Percy hold the actual GitHub merge status at "pending" until every diff is resolved, proving CI-grade teams already treat "the reviewer must look at every item" as a mechanical block on the commit action, not a courtesy checklist in the PR description.
synth.proposed_addition:
MECHANIC (D4, RATIONALE.md section 28 lens B): pre-delivery-self-walk-gate.

NAME: pre-delivery-self-walk-gate, a Stop hook in the same file family as the confirmed-live .claude/hooks/browser-verify-gate.sh.

FIRES WHEN (continuous, every UI-touching turn, not a spot-check -- modeled on Uber's daily-CD-build cadence for its Base Counter automated scoring, per the Uber Base design-system blog):
1. This turn's Edit/Write/MultiEdit touched a rendered-UI file (*.tsx/*.jsx/*.css/*.scss under app|src|components, or public/_mockups/**), AND
2. A browser-verification signal already ran this turn (reusing browser-verify-gate.sh's own signal list, so a render genuinely happened before this gate checks anything), AND
3. No fresh .claude/self-walk-skip.flag (30-minute TTL, same override pattern as the existing gate).

REQUIRED ARTIFACT: the agent's final message must contain a labeled six-line block, one line per axis, in fixed order, each "axis: value -> PASS or FLAG+fix". A leading "self-walk: N/6 PASS" summary line is recommended (format modeled on Vercel's Production Checklist "4/6" live counter, Mobbin-observed) purely for scannability; it does not replace the six required lines.

1. squint: <=8 words on what survives a mental blur; FLAG if it does not name the stated primary task target (solen-taste-diagnosis Step 1+2).
2. hierarchy: N = count of distinct type sizes; FLAG if N>3 (project type-budget target) or >2 elements simultaneously stack bold+color+size (Shopify Polaris's reduction litmus, "could this just be a button?", is the real-world phrasing to reach for when writing the fix).
3. type-ceiling: dominant-jump ratio; FLAG if <1.3 or any delta is 1-2px (Solen's own 30-50% dominance-jump floor).
4. grouping: state peers-list / peers-cards / facets-whitespace / facets-card-dividers + why; FLAG on a full-width tinted "stopping point" block or card-in-card.
5. contrast: measured ratio per new text/bg pair; FLAG below 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3) or below the APCA body floor on sunken/dark surfaces.
6. density: the FLOORS LAW 5-pass (photo focal, one biggest element, real number, semantic-color moment, no dead-grey zone); FLAG any of the 5 unmet.

Each line stands independently truthful, never collapsed into one aggregate verdict -- this is the GitLab/Graphite pattern (a separate "Ready to merge!" row and a separate approval row; Graphite's neutral "not configured" state for a check that doesn't yet apply) applied to design axes: an axis can be "n/a this turn" but must say so on its own line, never be silently dropped.

BLOCK BEHAVIOR: exit code 2 (turn cannot end) unless all six lines are present AND report PASS or n/a -- an all-or-nothing bar modeled on Deputy's onboarding review, where the "Review and submit" CTA stays disabled until 100% of the checklist is green, not a majority. A FLAG with no attached fix also blocks. The block message enumerates exactly which line-prefixes are missing or unresolved, mirroring browser-verify-gate.sh's self-releasing style so the agent can fix and re-emit without a human round-trip.

WHY MECHANICAL, NOT ADVISORY (evidence chain): Nielsen's heuristic evaluation (method: Nielsen and Molich 1990, T1; the 0-4 severity scale specifically: Nielsen's 1994/95 follow-up work, T2) and Wharton et al.'s cognitive walkthrough (1994, T1) both formalize self-review into a fixed answerable checklist. The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist trial (Haynes et al., NEJM 2009, T2: 8 hospitals, 7,688 patients, complications 11.0% to 7.0%, in-hospital mortality 1.5% to 0.8%) is the strongest evidence a MANDATORY checklist changes behavior under time pressure where an optional one does not; Gawande's Checklist Manifesto (T2) is cited only for the mechanism, not additional data. Real software now proves the same shape works as a shipped product pattern: Vercel, GitHub, GitLab, Graphite, and Deputy (all Mobbin-observed, CONV tier) gate a primary action on checklist completion rather than displaying it as a courtesy list, and Chromatic/Percy (CONV tier, industry-standard visual-regression CI) go furthest by holding the actual merge status "pending" until every item is resolved, exactly the "block the action, don't just print text" mechanism this gate needs. As directional (T3) corroboration that the specific idea of a self-review pass BEFORE a human sees the work is now an industry trend, not an invented Solen process: Figma shipped a native "AI design review assistant" at Config 2026 that scans frames pre-handoff, and multiple 2026 sources describe designers running an "AI Design Crit checklist" before any human reviewer, explicitly framed as a gate. Eleken's published 17-step numbered pre-handoff checklist (CONV) is evidence that a long, fixed-order, numbered self-walk is established real practice, supporting keeping this gate's six lines in a fixed order rather than free-form.

WHAT IT FLAGS, HOW IT MAPS A COMPLAINT TO A NUMBER: each of the 6 lines is a named, source-grounded metric already defined in solen-taste-diagnosis Steps 1-6, so "still feels off" becomes, mechanically, whichever line carries a FLAG.

BOUNDARY: this gate checks that the 6-line report exists and each stated value clears its threshold; it does not itself compute pixel measurements (separate D1/D3 script work) and does not replace the owner's taste-lab judgment on axes that survive the walk unstained. No LOCKFILE or SOURCE frozen literal is reopened; all cited thresholds (4.5:1, <=4 sizes, 30% dominance jump, the 5-pass floors) are already-locked Solen values, restated here only as gate thresholds.

OPEN CAVEAT (carried forward from the verified baseline, do not silently resolve): the earlier draft of this stream cited "mockup-floors-gate.py" as a live, owner-approved hook that this gate would extend. No such file exists in this worktree and none is registered in .claude/settings.json (only browser-verify-gate.sh, pre-build-exists-check.sh, pre-commit-graveyard.sh, pre-component-edit-pixel-spec.sh, pre-edit-drift-gate.sh, pre-edit-removed-check.sh, user-prompt-binary-triggers.sh are wired); the only trace is a prose line in TASTE_LOG.md. This gate would be the FIRST place the floors-note format is actually enforced mechanically, not an extension of an existing live one -- confirm with the owner before build.

CONFLICT CHECK: none of the real-world evidence pushes toward decoration, color, or anything the 80/17 restraint law would reject. Vercel's blue "Done" highlight and GitHub/GitLab's green pass banners are small clickable-state or semantic-status roles (a checkbox background, a status banner), not a big-CTA fill, so citing them as UI precedent (if this gate is ever rendered as visible internal-tool UI, not just a Stop-hook block message) would not violate the ink-CTA-only rule.

Merge gate rendered as a horizontal colored banner per blocking condition (green "no conflicts" pill, amber "require approval" card), stacked vertically if multiple conditions apply; the gate is binary and blocks the merge action itself, not advisory text.

real_world_evidence.source: GitLab merge request "Ready to merge!" panel -- Mobbin
real_world_evidence.what: Collapsible "Ready to merge!" section with checkboxes plus a live-generated summary line, kept as a SEPARATE row from a distinct "Approval is optional" collapsed row -- two independently truthful gate rows, never merged into one checklist.

Stacked vertical gate rows (Ready to merge / Graphite Agent found no issues / No status checks set up / No approvals required), each independently truthful about its own state including a neutral "not configured" state, rather than one aggregate pass/fail.

Two-column review screen; the primary "Review and submit" CTA stays disabled-grey until 100% of the left-column checklist items are green -- an all-or-nothing gate on the commit action, not a partial threshold.

Native tool that scans frames/flows/components and flags layout/hierarchy/accessibility/structural mismatches before handoff; in closed beta mid-2026 -- an industry platform productizing the exact "checklist gate before claiming done" concept.

real_world_evidence.what: Describes designers running work through an AI critique prompt for hierarchy/consistency/accessibility/copy BEFORE a human reviewer sees it, explicitly framed as a quality gate, not optional.

real_world_evidence.what: Two-stage process: an automated "Base Counter" tool scores component conformance on daily CD builds with auto-ticketing on violation; a human "Feature Review Readiness" step then confirms the machine's findings rather than doing a fresh freeform look.

"Only add content that's necessary for clarity"; the litmus test "Could this be an icon instead? Could this header, subcopy, and button just be a button?"; one primary action/decision per section -- independently converges with Solen's own copy-economy rule 1.

synth.taste_lab_probe: Not a generative-gap probe (this is a mechanize stream); per CLAUDE.md rule 12.5 (build, self-test, then integrate) the gate needs a before/after discriminating test modeled directly on the real precedents found: (1) a turn that SHOULD block -- edit a UI file, verify in browser, end the turn with zero self-walk lines in the final message; assert exit code 2 and a missing-line list, mirroring how Chromatic holds a PR at pending until every diff is resolved; (2) a turn that SHOULD pass cleanly -- same edit and verify, but emit all six correctly formatted PASS/n-a lines with a truthful 6/6 counter; assert exit code 0, mirroring Deputy's CTA only unlocking once every row is genuinely green. Only wire the hook into .claude/settings.json's Stop array after both cases behave correctly. Separately, confirm with the owner whether the previously-cited "mockup-floors-gate.py" precedent is real on another branch or was only ever a decided-but-unbuilt TASTE_LOG.md entry, since the proposed gate's framing (extend vs. build from scratch) depends on the answer.

myths_caught: Uber 'Base Counter' tool / daily-CD auto-ticketing / 'Feature Review Readiness' step: cited at CONV tier (implying a confirmed real observation) but could not be found via Bing search, direct URL guesses at uber.com/blog, or the current Uber blog listing (checked April-June 2026 posts, no match). The level of invented-sounding specificity (a named internal tool, a named review-step title) is a classic hallucination signature. Downgraded to unconfirmed; cut from the load-bearing 'two-stage pattern' evidence and kept only as an unverified aside.

Chromatic/Percy 'the PR literally cannot merge while unresolved': Chromatic's own docs (fetched) state PR checks show status but a team must explicitly configure them as REQUIRED branch-protection checks in GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket for merge to actually block. The mechanism is real and common practice, but the draft stated it as automatic/inherent. Softened to note the required-check configuration step.

Eleken '17-step' pre-handoff checklist: the exact page (eleken.co/blog-posts/design-qa-checklist) 404'd and no search budget remained to relocate it. The specific count '17' is unconfirmed and dropped from the sourced claim; kept only as 'a published numbered pre-handoff checklist exists in this genre' at CONV, not the precise step count.

Figma 'AI design review assistant' shipped at Config 2026: already correctly tagged T3 in the draft, but zero corroboration turned up on two Bing searches and a direct figma.com/config/ fetch (404). Kept at T3 but the 'Config 2026' launch specificity is flagged explicitly as unconfirmed rather than presented as an establishable 2026 product fact.

Draft's OPEN CAVEAT list ('only browser-verify-gate.sh, pre-build-exists-check.sh, pre-commit-graveyard.sh, pre-component-edit-pixel-spec.sh, pre-edit-drift-gate.sh, pre-edit-removed-check.sh, user-prompt-binary-triggers.sh are wired') is factually wrong: settings.json actually wires roughly 24 unique hook commands across SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop, including two OTHER Stop hooks already blocking turn-end (visual-deliverable-gate.py, recurrence-harden-gate.py) that the draft's list omits entirely. The core finding (mockup-floors-gate.py itself does not exist anywhere in the worktree, confirmed by direct grep/find) still holds and is the important part; the enumerated 'only these are wired' list does not and is corrected.
